outcome: Agents work from browser-delivered desktops that keep client data central, so onboarding no longer waits on shipping physical hardware.
overview: A business process outsourcer with distributed agents has a specific problem: client data must not sit on an agent’s device, agents join and leave in volume, and the endpoint estate spans whatever hardware people actually have. Nutanix Frame delivers desktops through a browser so the data stays central and the endpoint becomes a display. What determines success is not the desktop technology but the network between the agent and the desktop, and that is the thing to test before anything is committed.

benefits.text: Client data stays central; the agent’s device displays a session rather than holding data
benefits.limits: Data stays central only where local drive and clipboard redirection are disabled, which is a policy decision agents will notice

benefits.text: Agents can be onboarded and removed at the pace the business actually hires
benefits.limits: Provisioning speed depends on capacity being available; a fixed pool sized for average demand will not absorb a hiring surge

benefits.text: Endpoint hardware becomes largely irrelevant to the delivered experience
benefits.limits: The endpoint stops mattering; the network between agent and desktop starts mattering a great deal, and in many locations it is the binding constraint

residency: Desktops run where the platform is deployed, which can be on-premises or in a chosen cloud region; agent devices hold no client data by design

notFor.situation: A workforce with reliable managed devices and no data-residency constraint
notFor.why: Managed physical desktops are cheaper to run than a delivery platform where the constraints do not apply

notFor.situation: Agent locations where connectivity cannot sustain an interactive session
notFor.why: This is the binding constraint and no platform choice compensates for it

scope:
Model: Redington solutions engineering with an accredited Nutanix implementation partner · Duration: 8–12 weeks to a live pilot population with quality measured at agent locations
Support model: Vendor subscription support; Redington coordinates the vendor case. Optional managed desktop operations.
1) Assessment — agent locations and connectivity, workflow requirements, redirection implications
2) Design — hosting location, capacity model, redirection policy and quality measurement
3) Pilot — a population live including agents at the worst-connected locations
4) Roll out and hand over — remaining populations migrated, operations handed over
deliverables: Session quality at the worst tested agent location meets the agreed threshold
No client data is written to an agent device, verified by test with redirection disabled
An agent can be provisioned and de-provisioned within the agreed time
effort: 8–12 weeks to a live pilot population with quality measured at agent locations
